home.title: Build interfaces that make sense.
home.lead: Not a gallery of pretty screens — a living guideline. Each rule has a name, a why, and two interactive examples: one that works, and one that hurts.

foundations.title: Foundations
foundations.description: The tokens everything else is built on: space, type, color, motion.

components.title: Components
components.description: Buttons, fields, and surfaces people actually touch.

composition.title: Composition
composition.description: How pieces sit together on a page — hierarchy, density, air.

ux-principles.title: UX principles
ux-principles.description: Behavior under stress: errors, waiting, emptiness, access.

scale.title: Space on a 4/8 scale
scale.description: A shared scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24…) is a rhythm, not decoration. Random gaps force the eye to re-measure every block. Pick a step, then only use those numbers — even when a slider tempts you off-grid.
scale.goodHint: The gap snaps to the scale. Related tiles stay in one beat.
scale.badHint: 7px, 11px, 13px look 'fine' until you put them next to each other.

proximity.title: Related things sit closer
proximity.description: Proximity is meaning. A label belongs to its field because of the small gap between them — not because of a box. Equal spacing everywhere flattens the relationship and makes the form slower to parse.
proximity.goodHint: Tight inside a group, looser between groups. Drag to feel the grouping.
proximity.badHint: The same gap between label, field, and the next section. Nothing belongs together.

padding-vs-gap.title: Padding holds, gap separates
padding-vs-gap.description: Padding is the breath inside a surface. Gap is the distance between siblings. Using margin as a dump for both creates collapse bugs and uneven edges. Keep inner space on the container, sibling space on the stack.
padding-vs-gap.goodHint: One padding on the card, one gap between rows. The edge stays even.
padding-vs-gap.badHint: Each row brings its own margin. The last item and the border never agree.

scale.title: Radius is a scale too
scale.description: 6, 10, 16, 24, pill. Mixing a 3px chip with a 28px input on the same row reads as two products glued together. Radius tokens keep the family resemblance when sizes change.
scale.goodHint: Every corner comes from the same ladder. Tune the step, not a one-off.
scale.badHint: Each control invents a radius. The row feels like a collage.

proportional.title: Bigger surfaces, rounder corners
proportional.description: A 40px button with a 24px radius looks swollen. A large card with 4px corners looks clipped. Radius should grow with the element so curvature stays optically similar.
proportional.goodHint: Small control, small radius. Large card, larger radius. Scale the box and watch it hold.
proportional.badHint: A pill radius on a tiny chip and a sharp corner on a huge card — both look wrong.

pill-vs-form.title: Pills for tags, not for typing
pill-vs-form.description: A stadium shape says 'chip / filter / status'. A text field is a box you enter. Pill-shaped inputs hide caret position and feel like buttons. Keep forms quietly rounded; save the pill for things you tap, not things you type.
pill-vs-form.goodHint: The field is a rectangle. The tag next to it can be a pill.
pill-vs-form.badHint: Type into a stadium. The shape argues with the task.

hierarchy.title: One voice, several sizes
hierarchy.description: Hierarchy is a staircase: display, title, body, caption. If everything is 16px medium, the page has no entry point. Size, weight, and space do the work that color shouting cannot.
hierarchy.goodHint: Change the display size. Body stays readable; the title still leads.
hierarchy.badHint: Title, meta, and body share a size. You have to read to know what matters.

measure.title: Keep the line 45–75 characters
measure.description: The eye returns to the next line. Too wide and it loses the start; too narrow and it chops phrases. Measure is a reading tool, not a layout leftover.
measure.goodHint: Stay near 65ch. The paragraph is easy to scan.
measure.badHint: A full-bleed paragraph. Your eye swims to find the next line.

line-height.title: Leading is part of the typeface
line-height.description: Body copy wants ~1.5; display wants tighter. Cramped leading is not 'more content' — it is friction. Pair line-height with size, then stop tweaking per paragraph.
line-height.goodHint: Comfortable leading at body size. You can read a block without squinting.
line-height.badHint: Line-height 1.05 on body text. It looks like a screenshot of a bug.

tokens.title: Name the role, not the hex
tokens.description: Accent, surface, danger are roles. Hard-coded #E8A54B in twelve files cannot survive a theme switch. Tokens let dark and light share meaning while the paint changes.
tokens.goodHint: The same card in both themes. The accent is a token, so contrast holds.
tokens.badHint: A hex that looked fine on dark, now vanishes on light.

contrast.title: Contrast is a requirement, not a vibe
contrast.description: WCAG AA is 4.5:1 for body text. Pretty grey on pretty grey is still unreadable. Check contrast where people actually read — not on the Figma artboard at 200%.
contrast.goodHint: Move the sliders. The ratio updates; the text stays legal.
contrast.badHint: Muted on muted. Stylish, and unusable in sunlight.

not-only-color.title: Never encode meaning in color alone
not-only-color.description: Red error text disappears for a large part of color-blind users and for anyone on a greyscale Kindle. Pair color with an icon, a word, or a pattern. Color is a highlighter, not the message.
not-only-color.goodHint: Error has an icon and the word Error. Color is extra.
not-only-color.badHint: Only the border turns red. If you cannot see red, nothing happened.

elevation.title: Elevation is a short ladder
elevation.description: Rest, hover, overlay. Three steps are enough. If every card looks like a modal, nothing is lifted. Shadows should answer 'how close is this to me?', not decorate the default state.
elevation.goodHint: Hover the card. It steps up one rung, not ten.
elevation.badHint: A 40px blur on a list row. Everything claims to be a dialog.

vs-border.title: Borders for rest, shadows for lift
vs-border.description: A 1px border is cheaper and cleaner for resting surfaces. Shadows belong to things that float (menus, modals, dragged cards). Stacking both at rest makes a muddy edge.
vs-border.goodHint: Resting card: border. Lifted card: shadow. Try both states.
vs-border.badHint: Border plus heavy shadow plus inner glow. The edge is a noise floor.

optical-size.title: Icons share the optical size of the text
optical-size.description: A 12px icon next to 16px labels looks like a footnote. A 28px icon next to the same label looks like a different control. Match stroke and box to the type size they sit with.
optical-size.goodHint: Icon and label share a size. Change type size; the icon follows.
optical-size.badHint: The icon is a different scale. It reads as a separate object.

align.title: Align to the cap-height, not the SVG viewBox
align.description: Icons have optical padding in the file. Naive `align-items: center` can still look low. Nudge until the glyph and the word share a midline — especially in buttons and nav.
align.goodHint: Icon and word sit on one line. Nothing feels dropped.
align.badHint: The icon hangs below the label. You can feel the misalignment.

consistency.title: One family: stroke or fill, not both
consistency.description: Outline icons are one language; filled icons are another. Mixing them in a toolbar says 'we grabbed whatever was in the set'. Pick a style, a stroke width, and stay there unless the fill means selected.
consistency.goodHint: All outline, same stroke. Selected can fill — that is a state, not a mix-up.
consistency.badHint: Outline, filled, two-tone. A toolbar of coincidences.

duration.title: Short, honest durations
duration.description: 150ms for color, ~240ms for small movement, ~400ms for large panels. Longer than that is a performance. Users should feel response, not wait for choreography.
duration.goodHint: Click. The chip settles in a fraction of a second.
duration.badHint: A two-second bounce on a toggle. You start to doubt the click registered.

purpose.title: Motion has to mean something
purpose.description: Enter, exit, spatial change. If a button spins 360° on click, the motion is a joke sitting on the task. Animate the thing that changed, in the direction the user is going.
purpose.goodHint: The panel slides from the control that opened it.
purpose.badHint: Everything wiggles. Motion is noise, so real change is harder to see.

reduced.title: Honor reduced motion
reduced.description: Vestibular disorders, batteries, preference. `prefers-reduced-motion` is not a nice-to-have — it is a contract. Instant states, no parallax, no large travel. The UI still works; it just stops swimming.
reduced.goodHint: Toggle reduced motion. The state still changes; the travel disappears.
reduced.badHint: The animation always runs. The setting is theater.

hierarchy.title: One primary action per view
hierarchy.description: Primary, secondary, ghost. If three buttons shout at the same volume, none of them is a decision. Hierarchy tells the eye where the next step is — especially in a toolbar or a dialog footer.
hierarchy.goodHint: One filled button. The rest recede. Click around: the path is obvious.
hierarchy.badHint: Three primaries. Every action is 'the' action, so none is.

states.title: Buttons have states, not just a default
states.description: Hover, focus, active, disabled, loading. A control that only looks good at rest will feel broken the moment someone touches it. Disabled must not steal focus; loading must not look dead.
states.goodHint: Hover, focus, then trigger loading. The button stays the same object.
states.badHint: No focus ring, a grey that looks like a label, loading with no spinner.

vs-link.title: Buttons do things, links go places
vs-link.description: A button submits, opens, deletes. A link changes location. Using a button for navigation breaks open-in-new-tab. Using an anchor for actions breaks keyboard and crawlers. The element is the API.
vs-link.goodHint: Save is a button. Docs is a link — Cmd/Ctrl-click works.
vs-link.badHint: A span that looks like a button. You cannot tab to it, and it does not go anywhere.

labels.title: A label is not a placeholder
labels.description: Placeholders vanish on type, so the field loses its name. Labels stay. Hint text can live below. If the only name is inside the box, a filled field is anonymous.
labels.goodHint: The word Email stays while you type.
labels.badHint: Type once — the name is gone. Was this email or username?

errors.title: Errors sit next to the field that failed
errors.description: A toast at the top of a long form is a scavenger hunt. Put the message under the input, set aria-invalid, and move focus. Timing: after submit or on blur — not on every keystroke for format.
errors.goodHint: Submit. The field explains itself and keeps focus nearby.
errors.badHint: A generic alert far away. The inputs look fine. Good luck.

required.title: Mark required before the user fails
required.description: Surprise required fields are a trap. Mark them in the label, or mark optional if most are required. Do not wait for submit to reveal the contract.
required.goodHint: Required is in the label. You know before you try.
required.badHint: Empty submit. Suddenly five fields were mandatory.

one-job.title: A card has one job
one-job.description: Preview, choose, or contain a small form — pick one. A card that is a link, a menu, and a settings panel at once creates nested click wars and muddy scanning.
one-job.goodHint: The card opens the project. Actions live inside, after the choice.
one-job.badHint: Clicking the title, the star, or the card body all mean different things — accidentally.

nested-click.title: Do not nest interactive targets
nested-click.description: A link wrapping a button is invalid HTML and a keyboard maze. If the card is clickable, inner controls need their own hit area that stops propagation — or the card should not be a link.
nested-click.goodHint: Card click opens. The menu button is a separate target.
nested-click.badHint: A link around a button. Click, tab, and screen readers disagree.

focus-trap.title: Trap focus, dismiss with Escape
focus-trap.description: A modal is a short conversation. Focus enters, Tab cycles, Escape and the overlay close, focus returns. Without that, keyboard users fall into the page behind the dimmer.
focus-trap.goodHint: Open, Tab, Escape. You never lose where you were.
focus-trap.badHint: Focus sits on the page behind. The dimmer is decoration.

one-primary.title: One primary action in a dialog
one-primary.description: Confirm vs cancel. If both are primary, the destructive path is as loud as the safe one. Place the primary in a predictable spot; make destroy secondary or danger, never both at once as 'the' button.
one-primary.goodHint: Delete is danger. Cancel is quiet. Easy to back out.
one-primary.badHint: Two filled buttons. Fifty-fifty chance you pick the ruinous one.

keyboard.title: A menu is a keyboard surface
keyboard.description: Enter/Space opens, arrows move, Enter selects, Escape closes. If it only works with a mouse, it is a decoration. Typeahead helps when the list is long.
keyboard.goodHint: Open with the button, move with arrows, select with Enter.
keyboard.badHint: Hover-only. Keyboard and touch get nothing reliable.

right-control.title: Two options are not a dropdown
right-control.description: A select with Yes/No is a tax. Use a switch or segmented control. Dropdowns earn their keep at ~5+ options, or when the current value must stay compact.
right-control.goodHint: On/Off is a switch. You see the state without opening anything.
right-control.badHint: A select for two values. An extra click for no extra meaning.

numeric.title: Numbers align on the right
numeric.description: Magnitudes compare by the left of the digit column — which is the right edge of the cell. Left-aligned money is a word, not a quantity. Keep units in the header, not in every cell.
numeric.goodHint: Scan the column. 9 and 900 line up.
numeric.badHint: Left-aligned amounts. You have to read each one to compare.

sticky.title: Keep the header when the body scrolls
sticky.description: A table without a sticky header becomes a riddle after two screens. Pin the header (and the first column if rows are identity). The data can move; the legend cannot.
sticky.goodHint: Scroll the body. You still know which column is which.
sticky.badHint: The header leaves. Every row is unnamed numbers.

density.title: Pick a density and stay there
density.description: Comfortable for browsing, compact for finance. Mixing an airy header with cramped rows looks unfinished and wrecks scan lines. Density is a property of the table, not of each row.
density.goodHint: Toggle density. The whole grid breathes the same.
density.badHint: A padded header, tight rows, a wrapped cell. No scan line.

current.title: Show where I am
current.description: aria-current, a strong weight, a persistent mark. If every item looks equal, wayfinding is guesswork. The current item is not a hover state — it is location.
current.goodHint: The active item stays marked after you click.
current.badHint: Nothing is current. You infer location from the page title alone.

landmarks.title: Nav is a landmark, not a pile of links
landmarks.description: A nav with a name, a list, skip links. Landmark navigation is how assistive tech jumps. A header full of unlabelled divs is a maze with no doors.
landmarks.goodHint: This demo exposes a named nav. Jump tools can find it.
landmarks.badHint: Links in a div soup. No list, no name, no current.

max-width.title: Give the page a measure
max-width.description: Full-bleed everything is not generous — it is exhausting. A max-width on reading and forms keeps the eye from travelling. Full-bleed is for media and atmospheres, not for every paragraph.
max-width.goodHint: Stretch the column. Type stays in a readable measure.
max-width.badHint: The text follows the window. On a wide screen it becomes a horizon.

visual-order.title: Visual order should match DOM order
visual-order.description: CSS order and absolute placement can put the primary action first visually and last in the tab sequence. Keyboard users walk a different page. Layout with source, not with tricks.
visual-order.goodHint: Tab through. The path matches what you see.
visual-order.badHint: The button is on the left but last in the DOM. Tab jumps strangely.

one-h1.title: One H1 per page
one-h1.description: The H1 is the document's name. Multiple H1s, or a pretty div pretending to be a title, break outlines and SEO and the mental model of 'where am I'. Style can be loud; the outline stays strict.
one-h1.goodHint: A single page title. Subheads are H2.
one-h1.badHint: Three H1s. The outline is a pile of shouts.

not-all-bold.title: If everything is bold, nothing is
not-all-bold.description: Weight is a scarce resource. Bold the one thing that must be found in a skim. A page of 600-weight body text is a flat wall.
not-all-bold.goodHint: Only the title and the key number are heavy.
not-all-bold.badHint: Every line is semibold. Hierarchy collapsed.

consistent.title: Do not mix densities in one region
consistent.description: A marketing hero next to a spreadsheet in the same card is two products fighting. Keep a region at one density; change density across regions on purpose, with a seam.
consistent.goodHint: One block, one density. Toggle it as a whole.
consistent.badHint: Airy title, cramped list, a huge empty footer. Three products.

context.title: Density follows the job
context.description: Dashboards can be compact. Onboarding cannot. Copying a data-dense table into a first-run screen is cruelty. Match density to risk and familiarity.
context.goodHint: Same data, two jobs: browse vs edit. The spacing changes with the job.
context.badHint: Onboarding squeezed like a Bloomberg terminal.

grid.title: Align to a grid, not by eye
grid.description: A 4px or 8px grid is cheaper than optical guessing. Ragged left edges and mixed inset values look like a draft. Snap, then break the grid only for optical exceptions (icons, quotes).
grid.goodHint: Cards share a left edge. Shift the gutter and they stay a family.
grid.badHint: Each block has its own indent. The column wobbles.

long-text.title: Do not center long text
long-text.description: Centered headlines can work. Centered paragraphs force the eye to find a new start every line. Left-align body; center only short, ceremonial lines.
long-text.goodHint: The paragraph is left-aligned. Easy returns.
long-text.badHint: A centered wall of text. Every line is a new hunt.

proximity.title: Group by closeness, not by boxes
proximity.description: A border around everything is not grouping — it is noise. Related actions share a small gap; unrelated ones get a larger one. Boxes are a last resort.
proximity.goodHint: Save and Cancel sit together. Delete is further away.
proximity.badHint: Every control is equally spaced. No family, no exile.

cards.title: A card groups one idea
cards.description: If two ideas share a card, the border lied. Split or use inner hierarchy. Cards are chunks of meaning, not a skin for the whole page.
cards.goodHint: Two cards, two ideas. Easy to scan.
cards.badHint: Profile, billing, and danger zone in one rectangle.

cta.title: Let the call to action breathe
cta.description: A primary button jammed against a paragraph is easy to miss and easy to mis-tap. Space around a CTA is a frame. It is not 'empty'.
cta.goodHint: Increase the air around Publish. It becomes the destination.
cta.badHint: The button is glued to the copy. It looks like a footnote.

breathing.title: Empty pixels carry structure
breathing.description: Filling every gap with a widget is anxiety, not utility. Whitespace separates chapters. If the page has no rest, the user cannot decide where to look.
breathing.goodHint: Add space between sections. The page gains chapters.
breathing.badHint: Widgets packed edge to edge. No place to land.

critical-actions.title: Do not hide the job on small screens
critical-actions.description: If Publish is in a hover-only toolbar, mobile users cannot finish. Collapse chrome, not the task. Primary actions stay reachable — often at the bottom, in a thumb zone.
critical-actions.goodHint: Shrink the frame. Publish is still there.
critical-actions.badHint: The action lives in a hover menu. Touch has no hover.

touch.title: Hit targets are at least 44px
touch.description: Fingers are not cursors. 24px icons with 0 padding are a dexterity test. Padding can make a small glyph a large target without looking childish.
touch.goodHint: The control is 44px tall. Easy to hit.
touch.badHint: A 22px hit area. Misses become rage clicks.

immediate.title: Answer the click immediately
immediate.description: A press without a response feels like a dead control. Disable, spin, or optimistic-update within 100ms. The work can be slow; the acknowledgement cannot.
immediate.goodHint: Click Save. The button becomes Saving… before the result.
immediate.badHint: Click. Nothing. You click again and double-submit.

silent-fail.title: Failures must speak
silent-fail.description: A 400 with a still form is a lie. Show the error, keep the input, offer retry. Silence trains people to hammer the button.
silent-fail.goodHint: The request fails. A message and retry appear.
silent-fail.badHint: The spinner dies. The form looks successful. It is not.

looks-like.title: It should look like what it does
looks-like.description: A thing that looks like a label but acts like a button is a trap. Affordances are promises: raised = press, underline = go, caret = type. Break the promise and trust dies.
looks-like.goodHint: The control looks pressable and is.
looks-like.badHint: Plain text that deletes on click. You would never guess.

cursor.title: The cursor is part of the affordance
cursor.description: pointer on buttons and links, text on fields, default on static. A pointer on non-clickable cards is a lie; a default cursor on a button is a shrug.
cursor.goodHint: Hover the button vs the caption. The cursor tells the truth.
cursor.badHint: Everything is pointer. Nothing is trustworthy.

confirm.title: Confirm the destructive path
confirm.description: Undo is better than confirm, but if the action is irreversible, ask. The confirm must name the object. 'Are you sure?' is not a name.
confirm.goodHint: Delete names the file. Cancel is easy.
confirm.badHint: One click, gone. No name, no undo.

constraints.title: Make the invalid path hard
constraints.description: Disable the end date before the start date. Constrain input instead of scolding after. Errors that could have been prevented are a design failure.
constraints.goodHint: The second date cannot precede the first.
constraints.badHint: Any dates. Submit. Then a lecture.

skeleton.title: Prefer skeletons for known layout
skeleton.description: A spinner in a void says 'wait'. A skeleton says 'this is the page, incoming'. Use spinners for unknown duration or tiny actions; skeletons for screens with a shape.
skeleton.goodHint: The shape of the card is already there.
skeleton.badHint: A lonely spinner. Layout appears later and jumps.

layout-shift.title: Do not jump the layout
layout-shift.description: Images without size, late banners, fonts swapping — CLS is a shove. Reserve space. Users miss buttons that move under their finger.
layout-shift.goodHint: Toggle loaded content. The height stays.
layout-shift.badHint: Content arrives and shoves the button down.

explain-action.title: Empty is a next step, not a dead end
explain-action.description: No projects yet → why, and a button to create one. Empty is onboarding. A blank table is a shrug.
explain-action.badHint: No data. That is the whole message.

dead-end.title: Search empty still offers a path
dead-end.description: Zero results should suggest clearing filters, trying another query, or creating the missing thing. A sad illustration with no control is a wall.
dead-end.badHint: A void. Filters stay on. You are stuck.

focus.title: Focus must be visible
focus.description: outline: none without a replacement is a locked door. Keyboard users need a ring that meets contrast. If you restyle it, keep 3:1 against the adjacent background.
focus.badHint: Tab. You guess where you are.

icon-name.title: Icon-only controls need a name
icon-name.description: A trash glyph is not a name. aria-label, visually hidden text, or a tooltip that is also in the accessibility tree. Title attributes are a poor substitute.
icon-name.badHint: The button announces… button. Or nothing.

skip-link.title: Offer a skip link
skip-link.description: Repeated nav is a tax on keyboard and screen-reader users. Skip to content is the courtesy of a door past the lobby. This app has one — the bad example shows life without it.
skip-link.goodHint: The first Tab hits Skip to content.
skip-link.badHint: Twelve nav links before the article. Every page.
